name: PAD Amputation Disposition — Synthetic Data Module
remarks: SYNTHEA MODULE — pad_amp_dispo (data-generation-only, repo: pad-amp-dispo-synth)
Generates the synthetic OMOP CDM consumed by pad-amp-ed-desc (Strategus).
Post-amputation ED visit descriptive study.
Patients: adults with dysvascular/diabetic/wound-related major lower
extremity amputation (BKA / AKA / foot). Outcomes: 90-day post-discharge
ED visit (35%), and inpatient readmission (70% of ED visits are admitted,
plus 3% of the cohort readmitted without an ED visit; net ~27.5%).
Frailty burden: VA Frailty Index (30 deficits).
REFERENCE — VA Frailty Index:
Cheng et al., J Gerontol A Biol Sci Med Sci 2021. PMID 33693638.
doi:10.1093/gerona/glab071
GitHub: https://github.com/bostoninformatics/va_frailty_index
ICD-10 mapping file: icd_code_vafi_mapping.csv
CONCEPT CODE STATUS:
All SNOMED-CT codes in this module have been verified [vocab query]
against the live omop_vocab schema (2026-07-05). 7 codes were corrected
from pretraining errors during batch verification. Safe to use.
See module commit history for verification details.
Vocab verification date: 2026-07-05.
See CLAUDE.md Rule 1 — Concept ID Transparency.
CLINICAL PATHWAY OVERVIEW:
Phase 1  Eligibility     Age guard (min 50, cap 100); onset delay
Phase 2  Exposure: 3-way distribution — 30% PVD-only / 30% PVD+DM / 40% DM-only
Phase 3  Frailty         30 VA-FI comorbidity states (sequential)
Phase 4  Treatment       Oversampling branch (5% non-exposed / 95% exposed)
Phase 5  Pre-index       Delay: 7-90 days (urgent/semi-elective amputation)
Phase 6  Index           Inpatient admission + major amputation procedure
Phase 7  Recovery        Inpatient stay 7-21 days post-amputation
Phase 8  Observation     Post-discharge window: 10-83 days (→ 90-day total)
Phase 9  Outcome gate    35% fixed ED-visit incidence (RESEARCHER_ADJUSTS)
Phase 10 Outcome         ED encounter (visit_concept_id 9203 in OMOP)
VA-FI SCORING NOTE:
The VA-FI score = (count of present deficits) / 30.
Three deficit pairs require OR logic in workflow/08:
Gait: Cov_Gait_Onset OR Cov_GaitAtaxia_Onset = 1 deficit
Falls: Cov_Falls_Onset OR Cov_FallInjury_Onset = 1 deficit
Kidney: Cov_CKD_Onset OR Cov_KidneyProc_Onset = 1 deficit
See covariates/covariates.csv comments for implementation.
PVD NOTE:
Peripheral vascular disease prevalence is set to 1.00 (100%) because
every patient in this cohort has dysvascular disease as the indication
for amputation. The PAD exposure condition (Exposure_Condition_Onset)
captures this at the study entry level; Cov_PVD_Onset reinforces it
as a discrete VA-FI deficit record in the comorbidity window.
OVERSAMPLING:
5% non-exposed / 95% exposed. Descriptive study — near-universal
exposure (amputation) by design. Real-world non-operative rate in
this severity of PAD is <5%.
OUTCOME INCIDENCE:
0.35 (35%) is consistent with published 90-day ED visit rates after
major lower extremity amputation (RESEARCHER_ADJUSTS per pilot data).
2026-08-02 EXTENSION - non-home discharge outcome + three-score covariates.
Added: index discharge disposition (NUBC 01/03/62) driving the NHD outcome;
an AKA index arm alongside BKA; risk-score covariates for the Iannuzzi 2020,
Subramaniam mFI-5 and Kraiss sVQI-FS scores (tissue loss, PAOD, dependent
functional status, walking aid, wheelchair device, insulin); and a
preoperative clearance encounter carrying Hgb, creatinine, BMI/weight/height
and a recent CHF record. See per-state remarks for the measured baseline each
one addresses. All concept codes verified against omop_vocab 2026-08-02.
Entry point. All simulated patients pass through Age_Guard.
Minimum eligible age: 50 years. Major dysvascular amputation is rare
below 50; nearly all index events occur 50-90 years.
RESEARCHER_ADJUSTS: lower to 18 to include early-onset DM patients.
Random delay after age 50 before PAD diagnosis. Spreads cohort entry
across the study period (2017-2025). Range 0-30 years → index ages 50-80.
RESEARCHER_ADJUSTS: narrow range for specific age window.
Upper age cap: 100 years. Prevents simulation of implausibly aged patients.
RESEARCHER_ADJUSTS: change quantity to tighten eligibility window.
COHORT ENTRY DISTRIBUTION — dysvascular amputation indication mix.
30% PVD-only  (peripheral arterial disease, no diabetes at index)
30% PVD + DM  (combined dysvascular/diabetic indication)
40% DM-only   (diabetic indication, no documented PVD at index)
Proportions derived from institutional amputation registry.

OVERSAMPLING DECISION POINT
Descriptive study: near-universal exposure (amputation) by design.
5% non-exposed represents operative mortality before procedure / refusal.
RESEARCHER_ADJUSTS: real-world non-operative rate for this severity of
dysvascular disease is <5%. Increase only if including medical management.
Closes the outpatient evaluation encounter before inpatient admission opens.
Time from outpatient evaluation to amputation.
Range: 7-90 days — reflects urgent/semi-elective limb-threatening ischemia.
Truly emergent cases (acute limb ischemia) would be 0-2 days.
RESEARCHER_ADJUSTS: narrow to 0-7 for emergency presentation cohort.
Narrowed 7-90 -> 7-60 days on 2026-08-02 so that adding the 1-30 day
Preop_To_Index_Delay downstream keeps the total pre-index interval in the
same 8-90 day band this state originally documented.
PREOPERATIVE CLEARANCE VISIT - added 2026-08-02.
Exists to solve two timing problems that no probability change could fix:
1. mFI-5 scores CHF over a -30..-1 day window, but the Cov_* chain fires
7-90 days pre-index, so only ~18 of 379 patients had a CHF record
inside 30 days, and the count moved with the delay draw.
2. query_bmi_covariate_counts() resolves BMI as 'most recent direct
reading wins', and stock Synthea writes a direct BMI (LOINC 39156-5)
at essentially every wellness encounter - 358 of 379 index patients.
A low weight recorded earlier can never win that ordering.
Placing these events in a dedicated encounter a deterministic 1-30 days
before index satisfies both windows without compressing the 30 VA-FI
comorbidity onsets into one month or breaking the documented 7-90 day
urgent/semi-elective workup interval.

RISK-SCORE COVARIATE: anemia - two different scores, two thresholds.
Iannuzzi:  Hgb < 10 g/dL           (2 points)
Kraiss:    Hgb < 13 M / < 12 F     (1 point)
EVERY patient is measured, both arms, on purpose. Both scores set
missing_is_negative = FALSE for anemia, so an unmeasured patient is scored
UNKNOWN rather than not-anemic. Only 85 of 379 index patients had any Hgb in
the -365..-1 window before this state existed, which silently shrank the
denominator. A preoperative CBC is standard of care regardless.
The 30% low arm (5.5-9.9) satisfies both thresholds. The 70% normal arm
(10.0-17.0) additionally trips the sex-specific Kraiss threshold for the part
of its range below 13 / 12, giving a realistic combined sVQI-FS rate near 50%.

remarks: RISK-SCORE COVARIATE: underweight, BMI < 18.5 (Kraiss sVQI-FS, 1 point).
Measured 1 of 379 before this state existed.
WHY A DIRECT BMI OBSERVATION AND NOT A VitalSign STATE - two reasons:
1. Synthea's VitalSign state only calls person.setVitalSign(); it writes no
record at all, so it cannot produce a measurement row.
2. query_bmi_covariate_counts() resolves BMI in three tiers and gives
priority 1 to a DIRECT BMI reading (3038553 / 36304833), ordered by date
descending. Stock Synthea writes a direct BMI at every wellness visit, so
a low weight alone can never win the ordering.
Emitting a direct BMI here, 1-30 days pre-index, makes it the most recent
reading. Weight and height are emitted alongside so the tier-2 computed
fallback agrees with tier 1 for any consumer that ignores direct BMI.
Prevalence 10%. (RESEARCHER_ADJUSTS)

LOINC 39156-5 -> OMOP 3038553 [vocab query — 2026-08-02]. Normal/overweight arm, 19.0-32.0 kg/m2.

DISCHARGE DISPOSITION GATE - drives the non-home discharge (NHD) outcome.
Replaces the former single Index_Encounter_End, which carried no
discharge_disposition at all, so every index visit landed in OMOP with
visit_occurrence.discharged_to_concept_id NULL and the NHD outcome
measured zero.
All three branches re-converge on Post_Discharge_Observation_Delay so the
existing 90-day ED-visit and readmission outcome path is unchanged.
Marginal split (RESEARCHER_ADJUSTS): 65% home / 22% SNF / 13% IRF, i.e.
~35% non-home. Real-world NHD after major lower extremity amputation runs
higher (60-75%); 35% is a deliberate enrichment choice that keeps the
dataset balanced for BOTH the NHD outcome and the pre-existing ED outcome,
and matches the enrichment the sibling pad_amp_nhd module already uses so
the two synthetic datasets stay comparable.
LIMITATION: NHD and ED risk are independent here - a SNF-discharged patient
carries the same 35% ED risk as one sent home, which is clinically wrong
but consistent with this module's existing unconditional-incidence design
(see Outcome_Assessment remarks). To correlate them, split this into two
post-discharge paths with different Outcome_Assessment gates.

OUTCOME INCIDENCE GATE — 90-day post-discharge outcomes (ED visit + readmission).
Three-way marginal split over the full cohort:
0.35 (35%) — post-discharge ED visit (Outcome_Onset). Of these, 70% go on
to an inpatient readmission (see Post_ED_Readmission_Assessment).
0.03 (3%)  — inpatient readmission WITHOUT a preceding ED visit
(direct to Readmission_Encounter).
0.62 (62%) — no post-discharge outcome (Terminal).
Net readmission incidence ≈ 0.35*0.70 + 0.03 = 27.5% of the cohort;
ED visit incidence stays 35% (literature 25-40% after major LE amputation).
NOTE: unconditional incidence — VA-FI frailty burden does not adjust these
probabilities. RESEARCHER_ADJUSTS: edit the distributions below, and the
70/30 split in Post_ED_Readmission_Assessment, per pilot data.
